skill.name: sitemapkit
skill.description: Use SitemapKit MCP tools to find sitemap files, extract sitemap URLs, and crawl public site URL lists.
skill.summary: Discover sitemaps and extract public URL lists through the SitemapKit MCP server.
skill.author: 0nl1n1n

security_audit.summary: Most static detections are false positives from Markdown examples, package metadata, placeholder API keys, and manual MCP setup paths; no prompt injection was found. One low-severity finding remains for public website enumeration. A high-severity semantic finding remains because setup runs an unpinned remote MCP package with an API key.

remediation.suggestion: Include the MCP server source and built artifact in the marketplace submission, or pin the npm package version and publish checksums for review.

remediation.issue: API key handling is not documented in detail
remediation.suggestion: Document where SITEMAPKIT_API_KEY is sent, how it is stored, and how users can revoke or rotate the key.

remediation.issue: Setup examples use an unpinned npx command
remediation.suggestion: Use a reviewed version such as npx sitemapkit-mcp@1.0.0 in setup examples so users run a known package release.

remediation.issue: Public site enumeration can be dual use
remediation.suggestion: Add usage guidance that users should crawl sites they own or are authorized to audit, and should respect rate limits.

content.value_statement: Finding all public URLs for a site can be slow and inconsistent. SitemapKit guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code to discover sitemaps and extract URL lists.
actual_capabilities: Selects discover_sitemaps, extract_sitemap, or full_crawl based on the user request.
Finds sitemap files for a domain through the configured SitemapKit MCP server.
Extracts URLs from a specific sitemap URL.
Returns combined URL lists across discovered sitemaps.
Reports truncation and remaining quota metadata when provided.
Maps common API errors to clear user guidance.
limitations: Requires the SitemapKit MCP server and a valid SITEMAPKIT_API_KEY.
Results depend on SitemapKit plan quotas and rate limits.
full_crawl and discover_sitemaps use the domain and ignore path details.
Only returns data available through public sitemap sources and SitemapKit responses.

use_cases.title: Audit Public Site Coverage
use_cases.description: Find sitemap files and summarize the public URL inventory before an SEO audit.

use_cases.title: Prepare Migration URL Lists
use_cases.description: Extract sitemap URLs so redirects, tests, and content checks can start from a known page list.

use_cases.title: Map Content Sections
use_cases.description: Collect page URLs from a site and group them by visible sections for content planning.

prompt_templates.title: Find Site Sitemaps
prompt_templates.prompt: Find all sitemaps for https://example.com and summarize where each sitemap was found.

prompt_templates.title: Extract One Sitemap
prompt_templates.prompt: Extract the URLs from https://example.com/sitemap.xml and group the results by site section.

prompt_templates.title: Crawl a Domain
prompt_templates.prompt: Crawl https://example.com up to 5000 URLs. Tell me if results were truncated and report remaining quota.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Sitemap Coverage
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare sitemap coverage for https://example.com and https://blog.example.com. Highlight duplicate sections and missing sitemap patterns.

output_examples.output: Found three sitemap files: the main sitemap, a blog sitemap, and a product sitemap. Two were listed in robots.txt, and one came from a common sitemap path.
The sitemap contains 148 post URLs. Most are under the blog section, and recent entries include last modified dates.

output_examples.input: How many pages does https://example.com have?
output_examples.output: The crawl returned 1,000 URLs and was truncated. Increase max_urls to review more pages if your plan quota allows it.

best_practices: Provide a full URL with the protocol, such as https://example.com.
Use sitemap discovery first unless you already know the exact sitemap URL.
Check truncation and quota details before treating a URL list as complete.
anti_patterns: Do not assume a full crawl includes unlimited URLs across every plan.
Do not use a domain path with full_crawl and expect path-level filtering.
Do not use the tool to audit sites without authorization.

faq.question: Does this skill require an API key?
faq.answer: Yes. The SitemapKit MCP server requires SITEMAPKIT_API_KEY in the MCP client configuration.

faq.question: Can it work with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill is marked as compatible with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: What is the difference between discovery and extraction?
faq.answer: Discovery finds sitemap files for a domain. Extraction returns URLs from one known sitemap file.

faq.question: Can it crawl every page on a site?
faq.answer: It can request a full crawl through SitemapKit, but results may be limited by quotas, rate limits, or max_urls.

faq.question: Does it find private pages?
faq.answer: No. It works from sitemap data and public discovery sources available to SitemapKit.

faq.question: What should I do when results are truncated?
faq.answer: Increase max_urls if your plan allows it, then rerun the request and compare the reported totals.
